2607.25886.description: Evaluates whether LLM agents can diagnose capability gaps and iteratively improve training-data strategies for a fixed target model under controlled post-training infrastructure and budgets.
2607.25886.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks entangle research choices with optimization, serving, evaluation, and systems implementation, obscuring data-centric research ability. Controlled, auditable comparisons reveal whether agents learn from checkpoint feedback and retain gains across revisions.
2607.25886.decisionReason: RSIBench-Data defines a controlled, repeatable evaluation with fixed infrastructure, budgets, and official sandboxed evaluation for comparing data-centric research agents.

2608.18607.description: Evaluates reward models for joint video-audio generation against human preferences, using both in-domain and out-of-domain model comparisons. Includes a human-preference dataset and benchmark with clear scoring protocols.
2608.18607.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in evaluating alignment of reward models for joint video-audio generation, providing a standardized comparison path that goes beyond individual quality metrics to assess overall coherence and fidelity.
2608.18607.decisionReason: VA-Judger-Bench is a named benchmark with a defined evaluation protocol, publicly released data/checkpoints, and clear scoring contract for comparing reward models.

2608.18701.description: Benchmark for deformable-object manipulation with visuo-tactile data, featuring 4,000 expert demos and multi-view sensory data. Defines Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR) as a metric for physical interaction quality.
2608.18701.whyItMatters: Provides a resource for evaluating not just task success but quality of physical interaction, filling a gap in deformable-object manipulation benchmarks.
2608.18701.decisionReason: Named dataset and benchmark with clear evaluation protocol and public data availability, though code is not provided but dataset is accessible.

2608.18586.description: Diagnostic benchmark for handwritten OCR with six subtasks and 77.57K labeled images, evaluating MLLMs with five metrics.
2608.18586.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in OCR benchmarks by covering realistic handwriting scenarios, but without public artifacts, the reuse path is unclear.
2608.18586.decisionReason: No code or dataset links provided in the paper; unclear if the benchmark is publicly accessible for other teams.

2608.18595.description: Reproducible benchmark for LLM-based program repair in the Odin language, with frozen data, containers, validators, and audit manifests. Instances include regression tests and execution records.
2608.18595.whyItMatters: Extends program repair benchmarks to a systems language, providing a rigorous, reproducible evaluation protocol for LLMs.
2608.18595.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear release artifacts and reproducible protocol, including frozen data and containers.

2608.18704.description: Benchmark for multi-source memory fusion with synthesized scenarios and evidence-grounded questions.
2608.18704.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in evaluating memory systems for fragmented observations, but artifacts are not clearly available.
2608.18704.decisionReason: No code or dataset links provided; unclear if benchmark is publicly accessible.

2608.18937.description: Benchmark for medical multimodal understanding and generation with 12 tasks and over 6M instances.
2608.18937.whyItMatters: Provides a broad benchmark for medical UAG, but without public access details, reuse is unclear.
2608.18937.decisionReason: No code or dataset links; benchmark accessibility is not specified.

2608.18618.description: Hierarchical benchmark for dexterous manipulation in laboratories, with real-world and simulation platforms.
2608.18618.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in evaluation for lab automation, but artifacts are not clearly available for reuse.
2608.18618.decisionReason: No code or dataset links provided; unclear if benchmark is publicly accessible.

2608.18532.description: Diagnostic benchmark for hidden-state reasoning in long videos, with 1,427 video-QA instances.
2608.18532.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in evaluating spatiotemporal reasoning when objects are invisible, but public access is unclear.
2608.18532.decisionReason: No code or dataset links provided; unclear if benchmark is accessible.

2608.18752.description: GreekBarRetrieval is a public retrieval benchmark for Greek statutory articles, derived from GreekBarBench. It includes 283 bar-exam questions with case facts and 6,308 candidate statutes, evaluating retrieval of relevant legal texts for everyday language queries.
2608.18752.whyItMatters: This benchmark fills a gap in legal retrieval for Greek, providing a standardized test for evaluating and improving statutory retrieval systems. It supports citation-grounded legal question answering and enables comparison of retrieval methods in a low-resource language context.
2608.18752.decisionReason: Provides a public benchmark with defined data, protocol, and evaluation metrics; includes baseline experiments and is accessible via ArXiv. The paper does not specify an ongoing scoring service, but the dataset and protocol are reusable.

2608.18993.description: ForeSightGuide is an anticipatory framework for visually impaired assistance, using vision-language models to predict hazards and filter alerts. It introduces a dataset for benchmarking predictive capabilities, but the paper focuses on the framework rather than a standalone benchmark.
2608.18993.whyItMatters: The framework addresses the problem of cognitive overload in assistive systems by providing anticipatory guidance. The introduced dataset could support development, but the primary contribution is the framework itself.
2608.18993.decisionReason: The dataset is introduced as part of a framework validation, not as a standalone public benchmark with a clear scoring contract or reuse path. No official code or data link is provided.

2608.18423.description: FM-Bench is a long-horizon management benchmark where LLM agents run a football club for 20 in-game years, making decisions via 26 tools. It measures sustained decision-making with a deterministic engine, offering Solo and Arena tracks for evaluation.
2608.18423.whyItMatters: It provides a challenging evaluation for LLM agents on tasks with cumulative consequences and competing agents, going beyond isolated tasks. The benchmark includes a codebase for running Solo evaluations and a managed Arena, supporting model comparison and analysis of managerial behavior.
2608.18423.decisionReason: Explicitly designed as a benchmark with clear scoring, code availability, and instructions for running evaluations. The abstract and code repo confirm a public reuse path and ongoing scoring via Arena.

2608.18534.description: FinRCA-Bench is a deterministic synthetic benchmark for financial reconciliation and root-cause analysis, containing 2,250 cases across 14 tables with injected failures and legitimate exceptions. It evaluates evidence retrieval and reasoning independently.
2608.18534.whyItMatters: It separates evidence access from reasoning quality, addressing a common conflation in end-to-end financial AI evaluation. The benchmark provides ground truth and data generation code, enabling reproducible assessment of retrieval architectures.
2608.18534.decisionReason: Provides a public dataset and generation code, with clear evaluation labels and a documented protocol. The GitHub link and paper describe the benchmark's structure and use, making it reusable.

2608.18554.description: CentaurBench evaluates LLM capabilities in both automating tasks and augmenting another agent's performance across seven real-world tasks, using blind pairwise comparisons by an LLM judge panel.
2608.18554.whyItMatters: It highlights that automation ability does not predict assistance quality, offering a framework for evaluating models in roles they play in human-AI systems. The approach could inform better model selection.
2608.18554.decisionReason: The paper describes a framework and experiments, but lacks clear public artifacts or instructions for reuse at this stage. No code or data link is provided, making it difficult to verify reproducibility.

2608.18591.description: BudgetDoc is a multimodal benchmark for estimating LLM reasoning performance under different budgets, supporting a DRB estimator for dynamic allocation. It includes three document tasks.
2608.18591.whyItMatters: It addresses the cost and over-thinking issues in inference by predicting performance across budget levels, enabling compute-optimal allocation. The approach could improve efficiency in document tasks.
2608.18591.decisionReason: While named a benchmark, the primary contribution is the DRB framework and dataset; the paper does not provide a clear public reuse path or ongoing scoring, and no artifacts are linked.

2608.18710.description: CamWorldQA is a benchmark for perceptual quality assessment of camera-controlled video generation, with 720 videos and human-rated scores. It supports a proposed CWQA network.
2608.18710.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in VQA for camera-controlled generation, focusing on viewpoint consistency and motion coherence. The dataset could aid development of specialized assessment methods.
2608.18710.decisionReason: The dataset is introduced to validate the CWQA method, lacking a standalone public comparison path. No data or code links are provided, and the benchmark is primarily a probe for the proposed approach.

2608.18451.description: The paper proposes DCGCNet, a deep learning model for atrial fibrillation detection from ECG signals, achieving state-of-the-art results across cross-dataset and noisy conditions.
2608.18451.whyItMatters: It introduces a robust method for AF detection, addressing variable leads and noise, with potential clinical deployment. However, it is not a benchmark but a model contribution.
2608.18451.decisionReason: The abstract describes a method and evaluation, not a benchmark with a reusable protocol. No public artifacts are provided for comparison.

2608.18726.description: AtmosCoder-Bench evaluates LLM computation in environmental science by requiring models to write executable Python solve() functions, which are run in a sandbox and graded against certified ground truth with unit-aware numeric comparison at 5% relative tolerance.
2608.18726.whyItMatters: It makes calculation process visible, revealing that multiple-choice formats inflate accuracy and that many failures stem from inconsistent formula application rather than missing knowledge, highlighting the need for execution-grounded evaluation in quantitative domains.
2608.18726.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation object with a clear scoring contract (execution-grounded, unit-aware grading), publicly available code and result data, and a credible path for other teams to run it.

2608.18588.description: AppEval is a benchmark for mobile application repair across HarmonyOS/ArkTS, iOS/Swift, and Android/Kotlin, using native toolchains and a common schema for build, install, launch, and test.
2608.18588.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap between repository-level repair evaluation and mobile build-install-launch-test boundaries, where infrastructure failures can be mistaken for program failures, but current quantitative findings are Android-specific.
2608.18588.decisionReason: The paper describes a benchmark, but without audited iOS and HarmonyOS results, the scoring contract is not fully specified across platforms, and no public artifacts are provided yet, making it unclear for public reuse.

2608.18675.description: An empirical benchmark comparing nine deep learning models for smart meter energy forecasting on two public datasets, analyzing input length, prediction horizon, architecture, and computational cost.
2608.18675.whyItMatters: It provides insights into model performance and trade-offs for energy forecasting, but does not define a repeatable evaluation object with a comparable scoring contract beyond standard metrics.
2608.18675.decisionReason: This is an empirical study comparing models, not a named benchmark with a defined protocol and public comparison path for other teams to run.
